author: James
text:
85% of iPad owners use it for 3 things: YouTube, Netflix, and casual browsing.

That's a $450-1,300 device with window tiling that runs 4 apps simultaneously, a document
scanner built into the Files app, Apple Pencil handwriting that converts to typed text in real
time, a keyboard that turns into a trackpad with one finger hold, Sidecar that makes it a
second monitor for your Mac, Stage Manager for desktop-class multitasking, Quick Note
from any screen, drag-and-drop between apps, Split View for side-by-side work, and Apple
Intelligence features that summarize, write, and create from any text field  being used as a
$1,300 Netflix screen.

The iPad is the most capable tablet ever made. And most owners treat it like an iPhone with
a bigger display.

iPadOS 26 has been one of the most notable software updates for iPad users to date. Apple
upgraded the multitasking experience by offering a new Window Tiling feature that lets users open many apps simultaneously. Yahoo!

A creative director who replaced her MacBook with an iPad Pro 2 years ago told me: "The
iPad isn't a consumption device. It's a production device that 85% of owners use for
consumption. The same iPad that streams Netflix edits 4K video, designs presentations,
annotates research papers, runs 4 apps side by side, and functions as a second monitor for
a Mac. The hardware has been ready for years. The software caught up in 2025. The
owners haven't caught up yet."

Here are 11 iPad features that turn a Netflix screen into a productivity machine
